description: Author estimates on LIVE's Elo-like scale, based on the statements and solution requirements, not a paper-position formula. LIVE values take precedence when later published. Shared 2026 AMC 10/12 problems receive identical estimates. The 2026 AMC 10A estimates were reviewed problem by problem on 2026-11-11 after the owner sat the paper: #25 came down sharply and #8, #16, #18, #20 and #21 moved.

2026 AMC 10A, Problem 2: Recognize that the tax share uses the total as denominator.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 3: Similarity locates the diagonal intersection; shared-height areas finish.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 4: Average interior or signed exterior angles, including reflex angles.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 5: Recognize that appending the current mean leaves it fixed.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 6: Recognize a right triangle and diameter, then subtract area from a semicircle.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 7: Subtract linear equations and count positive splits.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 8: Take the favourable rounding endpoint of both the distance and the time, read 'possibly allow' correctly, and convert minutes to hours; the wording costs more solvers than the arithmetic.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 9: Match unequal corresponding sides of similar triangles without assuming the labels match.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 10: Combine the sum of squares with the median and solve the resulting ratio.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 11: Separate the cases where the LCM is the fixed number or the unknown.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 12: Reverse the stopping event into constraints on the final three socks.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 13: Total handshakes determine the sum; cross-club handshakes determine the product.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 14: Intersect all three quadratic triangle inequalities and enforce positivity.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 15: Find the inverse tree rule and run a subtractive Euclidean process.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 16: First minimize the capped score, then count the four extremal colour patterns; short once the minimum of 4 is found.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 17: Recognize the intersection as a smaller regular hexagon through inward distances.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 18: Shift an affine recurrence to its fixed point, then use integrality and strict decrease across ten halvings.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 19: Project a hemisphere-covering problem and balance extreme corner distances.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 20: Squarefree factorization into three factors: onto assignments of seven primes by inclusion-exclusion, divided by six because the sides are distinct.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 21: Only ten connected-triomino partitions exist, and a win forces the four X's to split two and two.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 22: An affine stretch turns ellipse tangency into circle-center geometry.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 23: Classify attainable count pairs by residues and handle the bounded endpoint cases.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 24: Divide a conjugate-value difference and count bounded integer coefficients.
2026 AMC 10A, Problem 25: A total-count equation and the bound from the room that starts with one nut give 95 at once; the feasibility schedule is not needed to choose the answer. Rated well below a usual last question after the owner sat the paper (2026-11-11).
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 7: Square the conjugate complex bases and use the cycle of powers of i.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 8: Convert unequal group percentages into a linear minimization with bounds.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 9: Keep the zero-factor branch and the denominator restriction while counting roots.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 12: Recognize a covering of all residue classes through the complement.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 13: Uniform random placements and distinct rolls reduce to one increasing order.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 14: Match a rotated box's ordered dimensions with the interior dimensions.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 15: Use a trigonometric product identity, then bound a logarithm's floor.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 18: Translate three section radii into squared distances to perpendicular planes.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 19: Factor a trigonometric sum and count all distinct branches.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 21: Translate six area lower bounds into a homothetic hexagon and an area ratio.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 22: Build and evaluate an ordered unary/binary-tree convolution recurrence.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 23: Telescope an infinite product and invert an algebraic number modulo its cubic.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 24: Model two corner-circle radii and external tangency, then select the feasible root.
2026 AMC 12A, Problem 25: Combine prime-power root counts, CRT and a minimal-product comparison.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 1: A sharp quadrilateral angle bound requires both a counting argument and a limiting example.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 2: Equal-area pieces reveal a ratio; perpendicular lines then force special-triangle similarity.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 3: Identify the envelope of a family of circles and decompose its tangent-bounded region.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 4: Exploit two parallelogram symmetries, similar triangles and two admissible area-ratio roots.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 5: A reflection reveals a tangent; chord geometry then requires recognizing the two positions.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 6: Find and bound both extremal enclosing-circle configurations for a closed chain of disks.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 7: Recognize equal reflected circumcircles and an anticomplementary-triangle homothety.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 8: Combine orthocenter/circumcenter coordinates with the perimeter's ellipse.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 9: Constrain an oblique plane by equal edges, solve its section and recover area from projection.
2019 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 10: Track repeated external-square constructions and multiple polygon-area contributions.
2019 HMMT February Algebra and Number Th: Check the small sums of two palindromes and rule out one two-digit value by cases.
A tower of powers of two; only exponent arithmetic, but three levels deep.
Notice the two shifted quantities are reciprocals, so sum equals product, then use the square and cube identities.
Guess the closed form from the binary expansion, prove it by induction, then sum the solutions under a bound.
Three products of an arithmetic and a geometric term force a quadratic for the ratio; two cases to compare.
Turn remainders by irrational moduli into a chain of inequalities between multiples of two square roots, then count.
Symmetrize a triple sum over the six orders of its variables so the fraction collapses to a product of geometric series.
A Dirichlet square root of the constant function: prime powers by a generating function, then multiplicativity.
The possible multipliers are the eigenvalues of the hypercube; found by summing the conditions over nested half-cubes, with a construction for each.
A radical recurrence hides a linear one; proving it needs a Vieta-style argument, and the sum then telescopes.
2019 HMMT February Combinatorics, Proble: No palindromic block forces every letter to differ from the two before it, so the word is one pattern repeated.
Restate the condition on the three hidden dice, then a short conditional count.
A symmetry shows neither player can gain an edge, so the game is about minimizing ties.
The expected count is multiplied by a fixed factor each round, by conditioning on the current count.
Periodicity and reflections cut a walk on the plane to a few states, some settled by symmetry, the rest by linear equations.
Split the reflections by axis, pair them up, and count the sequences that return, case by case.
A reinforced vote: the distribution of one candidate's count stays linear in the count, proved by induction.
Cases on the shape of the factorization; the divisor lattice decides which divisors must take distinct colors.
Write the entries in binary: a filling is three independent placements of non-attacking ones.
A change of coordinates turns the moves into independent sign choices in four coordinates.
2020 HMMT February Algebra and Number Th: Substitute a root into the cubic; Vieta's formulas give the same in one line.
Clear denominators and factor, then match coprime factors of a fixed product.
Unwind three nested logarithms in two bases to a quadratic in the innermost one.
Count each prime's contribution to a double sum, which turns it into geometric series.
Track when the digit counts of ten powers jump; counting the jumps is counting reduced fractions.
Find the minimal polynomial of the root sum, then a size argument shows coefficients below 9 cannot cancel.
A prime divisor of the denominator below n is impossible; for a prime denominator Wilson's theorem reduces the factorial.
Build an auxiliary polynomial with known roots from the interpolation data and read off the value.
Write the polynomial of pairwise products of roots through the original polynomial and evaluate with Vieta.
Count the image of the map h to h^101 - h on polynomials modulo x^1001 - 1 over the field with 101 elements.
2020 HMMT February Combinatorics, Proble: A majority condition forces a face of one color; a few cases.
By the Chinese Remainder Theorem a number up to 210 is its three remainders; choose them distinct.
Each 2-by-2 block holds at most two rainbow L-trominoes by pigeonhole, and a coloring reaches the bound.
Choose the squares as a matching of rows to columns, split by parity of rows and columns.
The expected count is the total length of all intervals over 1000; the lengths add level by level.
Each move flips all three letter counts' parities, which decides when one letter can remain.
A square product appears once the exponent vectors mod 2 become dependent; sum the probabilities of lasting k draws.
Replace each random point by a random equilateral triple, reducing to choosing among twelve points.
Recast as colorings of a ten-cycle in two interleaved five-cycles, then count up to rotation.
The difference grows only at zero, so sum the chances of being at zero, a central-binomial generating function.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 1: Place the shared vertex in each possible way; the triangle is isosceles on a unit base.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 2: A long diagonal of the hexagon is parallel to a side of the triangle, giving similar triangles.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 3: Trace the partner endpoint as one endpoint moves, and maximize the length over the cases.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 4: Equal tangent lengths from each vertex and a right triangle relate the two radii.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 5: Six rotated copies of the region form a larger hexagon with a circular hole.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 6: The incenter is equidistant from the three new points, by congruent right triangles on the tangent lengths.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 7: Express the tangent lengths through the distance from the center to the chord, then solve the given ratio.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 8: The bisector also bisects the angle between the altitude and the diameter; similar right triangles give a quadratic.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 9: Invert about the incircle of the centers' triangle; Descartes' theorem gives the radius from the two tangent circles.
2020 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 10: Invert so the two circles become concentric; a closed chain of 2020 tangent circles fixes the ratio of radii.
2018 HMMT February Algebra and Number Th: Find the unique horizontal level of a three-piece absolute-value graph.
A substitution turns a nested exponential equation into t^t; check uniqueness.
Square residues remove the floor, then prime factor pairs leave four candidates.
Divide by the product of the distinct primes and use integrality to restrict each prime.
Optimize distinct powered roots through inverse permutations and a primitive-root parity obstruction.
Convert three trigonometric terms into unit vectors, locate an extremal boundary, then recover a coordinate.
Separate large and small states and count the significant histories by a Fibonacci recurrence.
Decompose sum-and-OR outputs bit by bit and identify the only collision at each bit.
Evaluate a quartic at negated roots, simplify the ratio, and check an attainable bound.
Bound possible low-degree integer factors, discard vanishing cases, and combine cyclotomic residue events in a limit.
2018 HMMT February Combinatorics, Proble: Two grid entries determine the rest through row and column congruences.
Separate the three carry patterns between consecutive five-digit palindromes.
Corner constraints force the coloring into a few complete patterns.
Odd changes of direction are equivalent to opposite first and last steps.
Condition a stopped sequence on avoiding the unwanted color before recognizing the waiting-time law.
Analyze simultaneous optimal choices and induct on the rectangle dimensions.
Find and count the initial-position restrictions that make the incomplete sorting schedule succeed.
Recognize valid cut positions as indicators and sum their permutation probabilities.
Apply inclusion-exclusion to digit positions equal to the total residue, treating the full intersection separately.
Bound a boundary graph by degrees, rule out equality by parity, and construct a near-extremal coloring.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 1: Recognize the right triangle and use the perpendicular-bisector similarity.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 2: Intersect the two triangle-inequality intervals and check degenerate endpoint attainability.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 3: Check all three possible placements of the given angle and eliminate invalid quadratic roots.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 4: Use a hinged face as a tetrahedron base and maximize its perpendicular height.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 5: Combine the diameter, bisected arc, equal areas and a center-to-chord similarity.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 6: Infer two coefficients of a prescribed area formula from continuous endpoint configurations.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 7: Optimize the average of a piecewise-linear section length over a variable interval.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 8: Recognize a harmonic configuration and its polar, then compute a tangent power.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 9: Use Euler counting for regions and indicators for crossings of nonadjacent random chords.
2018 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 10: Transfer a constant ratio of powers through a circle pencil, then evaluate the second line intersection.

Change ordered exponents into positive gaps and separate a triple geometric series.
Specialize a multiplicative functional equation on the reals until its values are forced.
Repeated divisibility peels off a high power before a size bound leaves two cases.
Recognize a weighted divisor sum as a multiplicative convolution and evaluate on five primes.
Turn 2016 prescribed values into roots of an auxiliary polynomial, determine its residual linear factor, and bound a harmonic sum.
Build a sequence of sharp square completions and verify the extremal coefficient.
Reduce integral quadratic pairs by descent, then generate the two bounded chains.
Use Fibonacci roots in a quadratic finite field to bound the period and rule out a smaller power of two.
Reduce a periodic functional equation to residue classes and count compatible labels on the squaring graph.
2017 HMMT February Combinatorics, Proble: Count the feasible ordered sums of three ten-sided dice.
Use last digits and divisibility by three to force a fixed number of summands.
Compare sums in residue classes of jars, prove an upper bound, and exhibit an attaining schedule.
Separate the possible walk lengths and count the choices of higher-labeled destinations.
Split on the unique allowed failure of decreasing order and remove the fully decreasing overlap.
Guess and prove the exact law of a reflected walk with a holding state at zero.
Strip forced partners until the bipartite graph consists of cycles, then count possible matching totals.
Filter every vertex degree modulo four in a random graph through a multivariate product.
Bound total pairwise symmetric differences and attain equality with binary linear functionals.
Move a local forbidden-switch window by a bijection, then count constrained ballot paths.

2017 HMMT February Geometry, Problem 2: Turn equal perimeters into a fixed side sum, maximize the product, and compare the three vertex choices.
